newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Wage agreements key to future Irish success - report.
newsitem.headline: Wage agreements key to future Irish success - report.

text.p: Ireland faces the challenges of promoting competitiveness, cutting unemployment and reducing inequality and a national wage agreement is the most effective means of achieving these aims, a report said on Tuesday.

The National Economic and Social Council (NESC), which includes representatives from government, business and trade unions, said a negotiated social partnership was "the approach most likely to yield appropriate settlements across the economy".

"Negotiated social partnership programmes are a most effective mechanism for developing Irish competitiveness and social cohesion in the current global context," the NESC said in its report, Strategy into the 21st Century.
It recommended real tax reductions of at least 0.5 percent of GDP each year over the years 1996 to 2000, while current public expenditure should be limited to a two percent real increase.
The NESC also recommended a gradual reduction in the public financial deficit to not more than 1.5 percent between 1997 and 1999, and a debt/GDP ratio of 70 percent by 1999.
A debt/GDP ratio of 60 percent could be achieved early in the next century, it said.
The priority for income tax reform was reduction of the tax burden for lower-to-middle-income earners, the NESC said.

"On corporation tax, the objective should be to secure the maintenance of the 10 percent rate and to progressively reduce the standard rate, while also reducing the tax burden on small business," it said.
